Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

💡 **SUGGESTION:** The relative link `[ws-doctor.spec.md](ws-doctor.spec.md)` in the Related list is broken in this registered plan copy: it resolves to `.agents/plans/enable-auditing/ws-doctor.spec.md`, which does not exist (the directory contains only this file). The identical link works in the spec of record at `.agents/specs/enable-auditing.spec.md` because `.agents/specs/ws-doctor.spec.md` exists — the link was copied verbatim into a different directory without adjusting the relative target. Anyone following the reference from the plan artifact lands on a 404.

**Correção sugerida:**

```diff
-- Related: [`ws-doctor.spec.md`](ws-doctor.spec.md) (static diagnose), `ws-check-harness`, `ws-fable-judge`, `ws-multi-spec`, `ws-github-provider` (issue creation via `gh` when user accepts).
+- Related: [`ws-doctor.spec.md`](../specs/ws-doctor.spec.md) (static diagnose), `ws-check-harness`, `ws-fable-judge`, `ws-multi-spec`, `ws-github-provider` (issue creation via `gh` when user accepts).
```

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 3/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: directory listing of `.agents/plans/enable-auditing/` shows only `step-00-enable-auditing.spec.md`; `ws-doctor.spec.md` exists only at `.agents/specs/ws-doctor.spec.md`. The spec file line 90 contains `Related: [ws-doctor.spec.md](ws-doctor.spec.md)`. 2. Scenario: a maintainer opening the registered plan copy clicks the link to review the related static-diagnose spec and gets a missing-file 404. 3. Protection: the plan/spec artifacts are not covered by the ws-doctor link checker (it scans skills root and hubs only, not `{plansDir}`), so no automated gate catches it. 4. Discards: considered whether the link is intended as a bare filename reference — the markdown syntax makes it a navigable link, and the sibling file in the same PR (`.agents/specs/enable-auditing.spec.md`) resolves, so the discrepancy is real.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/plans/enable-auditing/step-00-enable-auditing.spec.md, /.agents/specs/enable-auditing.spec.md, /.agents/specs/ws-doctor.spec.md
</details>

Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

💡 **SUGGESTION:** This boundary table links a Workflows-package skill to an Extra-package skill via a real relative path. `ws-doctor` ships in the Workflows package (`bin/skill-dependencies.json` `packages.workflows.skills`), while `ws-show-harness` ships only in the Extra package (`packages.extra.skills`). In a Workflows-only install (the default `--package workflows`), `ws-show-harness` is absent, so `../ws-show-harness/SKILL.md` is a broken link in the shipped body — and, ironically, the doctor's own path scan will then report its own SKILL.md as a missing reference on the very surface it is meant to keep clean. The repository explicitly isolates Extra skills to avoid phantom routes in Workflows-only installs (root AGENTS.md scope note; ws-shared/AGENTS.md `### Extra package (optional)`), and no other Workflows skill links to an Extra skill (ws-check-harness and ws-check-workflows do not).

**Correção sugerida:**

```markdown
| Skill | Use when |
|-------|----------|
| **This skill** | Broken paths after token expand, missing launchers / scripts, parse failures, live `config.json` summary, missing companion refs |
| [`ws-check-harness`](../ws-check-harness/SKILL.md) | Phases 0-5c integrity, routing, portability, digests, topology |
| `ws-show-harness` (Extra package) | What is active in the **current session** |
```
(Keep the boundary note but drop the relative link so Workflows-only installs have no phantom path.)

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 6/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: bin/skill-dependencies.json lines 25-66 put ws-doctor in workflows and lines 72-75 put ws-show-harness in extra; root AGENTS.md scope note states Extra skills are 'absent from Workflows-only installs' and that consumer routes keep them isolated 'so Workflows-only installs avoid phantom routes'; grep across `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` shows only ws-doctor references ws-show-harness (line 28); ws-check-harness and ws-check-workflows bodies contain no Extra-skill links. 2. Scenario: consumer installs `--package workflows`; `ws-show-harness` is not copied; doctor scans its own SKILL.md, resolves `../ws-show-harness/SKILL.md` against `.agents/skills/ws-doctor/`, finds nothing, and emits a false path-error finding for its own body. 3. Protection: `ws-check-harness` runs in this repo where ws-show-harness exists on disk, so the link resolves and no phase flags it; the workflows-only install layout is never audited. 4. Discards: the row is prose (a 'use when' boundary note) and could be considered non-routing — but it is a literal file path in the shipped body, which is exactly the phantom-path class the harness avoids; moving the mention to ws-shared/AGENTS.md Extra section would preserve the note without the broken link.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/skills/ws-doctor/SKILL.md, /bin/skill-dependencies.json, /.agents/skills/ws-shared/AGENTS.md, /.agents/skills/ws-check-harness/SKILL.md
</details>

<!-- resolution-reply -->

Fixed: boundary table now names ws-show-harness (Extra package) without a relative link, avoiding Workflows-only phantom paths.

Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

💡 **SUGGESTION:** The template-detection predicate tests the same condition twice: `t.includes('\u2026')` appears as both the second and third clause. The adjacent `asciiSafe` helper (line 129) shows the author distinguishes `'...'` (three ASCII dots) from the single ellipsis character `\u2026`, so the duplicated clause likely hid a third intended variant (for example the two-dot leader `\u2025` or midline ellipsis `\u22EF`). The redundancy has no runtime impact today, but it masks the lost clause and invites a future fix in the wrong place.

**Correção sugerida:**

```js
if (t.includes('...') || t.includes('\u2026') || t.includes('\u2025') || t.includes('\u22EF')) return true;
// Or, if no extra variant is intended, simply drop the duplicate:
// if (t.includes('...') || t.includes('\u2026')) return true;
```

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 3/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: doctor.js line 226 reads `if (t.includes('...') || t.includes('\u2026') || t.includes('\u2026')) return true;` — third clause identical to second; asciiSafe line 129 maps `\u2026` to '...' separately from the ASCII '...' case. 2. Scenario: no functional failure — the duplicate is idempotent; the risk is a missed ellipsis-like variant because the intended clause was overwritten by copy-paste. 3. Protection: all smoke tests pass regardless, so nothing guards the predicate's completeness. 4. Discards: it is not a crash or misclassification (the condition still returns true for ellipsis-containing strings), so severity is minimal; it is still a provable defect in new code rather than style preference.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/skills/ws-doctor/scripts/doctor.js
</details>

<!-- resolution-reply -->

Fixed: removed duplicate \u2026 clause in isTemplateOrGlobPath.

Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

🛑 **CRITICAL:** ws-audit was added to packages.workflows.skills but no dependency edge was added for it in any orchestrator closure, in either the bin graph or the packaged ws-shared graph. All three orchestrators dispatch it at runtime: ws-spec-to-pr/SKILL.md loads it at bootstrap, STEP-DISPATCH.md appends findings via it after every step's update_state and runs the end-of-run upstream-issue gate through it, ws-spec-to-pr-lite step 9 instructs following it, and ws-multi-spec makes every worker follow it. Per check-harness Phase 4b rule 6 and root AGENTS.md, every dispatched skill id must appear in dependencies["<orch>"] directly or transitively; a missing edge is critical because a selective install of an orchestrator would not pull ws-audit, so enabling defaults.enableAuditing then points the STEP-DISPATCH recipe at an uninstalled skill - precisely the silent phantom-route failure the audit feature was designed to surface. Note ws-check-harness and ws-check-workflows are already in the ws-spec-to-pr closure, so the graph convention for harness skills exists; ws-doctor (a leaf harness skill, same tier) is likewise absent.

**Correção sugerida:**

```json
// bin/skill-dependencies.json AND .agents/skills/ws-shared/skill-dependencies.json
"ws-spec-to-pr": [
  "ws-write-spec", "ws-classify-complexity", "ws-write-plan", "ws-interview",
  "ws-plan-to-tasks", "ws-implement-tasks", "ws-verify-plan", "ws-code-review",
  "ws-testing", "ws-ship-pr", "ws-fix-pr", "ws-goal-fix-pr",
  "ws-update-plan-implementation", "ws-github-provider", "ws-azure-devops-provider",
  "ws-local-spec-provider", "ws-check-harness", "ws-check-workflows", "ws-audit",
  "ws-tdah", "ws-karpathy-guidelines", "ws-spec-format", "ws-goal-loop",
  "ws-self-learning", "ws-changelog", "ws-configure-project", "ws-spec-index",
  "ws-senior-developer", "ws-patterns-backend", "ws-patterns-frontend"
],
"ws-spec-to-pr-lite": [
  /* ...existing entries... , "ws-audit" */
],
"ws-multi-spec": [
  "ws-spec-to-pr", "ws-spec-to-pr-lite", "ws-classify-complexity", "ws-ship-pr",
  "ws-goal-fix-pr", "ws-audit", "ws-tdah", "ws-karpathy-guidelines"
]
```

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 9/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: read bin/skill-dependencies.json (dependencies section lines 82-203: ws-spec-to-pr, ws-spec-to-pr-lite, ws-multi-spec arrays contain no ws-audit or ws-doctor; ws-check-harness/ws-check-workflows ARE in ws-spec-to-pr lines 100-101), .agents/skills/ws-shared/skill-dependencies.json (identical gap), ws-spec-to-pr/SKILL.md line 80, ws-spec-to-pr/STEP-DISPATCH.md line 46, ws-spec-to-pr-lite/SKILL.md line 39, ws-multi-spec/SKILL.md line 51, ws-check-harness/PHASES.md line 332 ('Missing id → critical'), root AGENTS.md dependency-graph rule. 2. Scenario: selective install of ws-spec-to-pr (installer installs orchestrator + declared closure only) + config defaults.enableAuditing: true → bootstrap 'load ws-audit' and per-step append instructions reference {skillsRoot}/ws-audit/... which is not installed → broken or silently-skipped audit, hiding exactly the skill-body defects the feature must record. 3. Protection: npm run test covers installer/integrity/tree, not closure completeness of dispatched skills; the PR description claims test/verify-integrity/smoke but not a green ws-check-harness Phase 4b. 4. Discards: considered that ws-audit is opt-in (conditional) - the harness rule has no conditional carve-out and STEP-DISPATCH unconditionally references the skill id when the flag is on; considered ws-doctor as equally critical - it is not dispatched by orchs, so it is referenced here only as a secondary consistency note.

**Caminhos analisados:** /bin/skill-dependencies.json, /.agents/skills/ws-shared/skill-dependencies.json, /.agents/skills/ws-spec-to-pr/SKILL.md, /.agents/skills/ws-spec-to-pr/STEP-DISPATCH.md, /.agents/skills/ws-spec-to-pr-lite/SKILL.md, /.agents/skills/ws-multi-spec/SKILL.md, /.agents/skills/ws-check-harness/PHASES.md
</details>

<!-- resolution-reply -->

Fixed: added ws-audit to ws-spec-to-pr, ws-spec-to-pr-lite, and ws-multi-spec dependency closures in bin and ws-shared skill-dependencies.json.

Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

⚠️ **WARNING:** ws-audit is now loaded and dispatched at runtime by ws-spec-to-pr, ws-spec-to-pr-lite and ws-multi-spec (documented in their SKILL.md bodies and in STEP-DISPATCH.md), but it was not added to the dependencies closure of any of those orchestrators in this dependency graph. The harness contract treats orchestrator-dispatched skills missing from the closure as critical (check-harness PHASES.md Phase 3 item 6 and ws-check-workflows SKILL.md section 3 both assert this closure), so the harness gates this PR relies on would not be green, and a selective install of the orchestrator without ws-audit (or a cascade uninstall) leaves a workflow that references a skill outside its declared closure.

**Correção sugerida:**

```diff
--- a/bin/skill-dependencies.json
+++ b/bin/skill-dependencies.json
@@ dependencies["ws-spec-to-pr"] @@
       "ws-check-harness",
       "ws-check-workflows",
+      "ws-audit",
       "ws-tdah",
@@ dependencies["ws-spec-to-pr-lite"] @@
       "ws-local-spec-provider",
+      "ws-audit",
       "ws-tdah",
@@ dependencies["ws-multi-spec"] @@
       "ws-goal-fix-pr",
+      "ws-audit",
       "ws-tdah",
```
Apply the same three additions to the packaged mirror `.agents/skills/ws-shared/skill-dependencies.json`, then run `npm run generate-integrity` / `npm run verify-integrity` and re-verify with `ws-check-harness` and `ws-check-workflows` (both must report 0 critical).

<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

⚠️ **WARNING:** The ws-audit orchestrator recipes instruct passing JSON payloads directly as inline shell arguments (`--session '{...}'`, `--finding '{"step":"4",...}'`, and the same for finalize/has-errors/draft-issue). This is exactly the pattern the hub's own cross-platform guidance forbids: ws-shared/AGENTS.md § Cross-platform shell & encoding rule 1 says never build scripts with embedded quotes/JSON via shell redirection or heredocs, and rule 2 says when a command needs nested quotes (JSON payloads), write a short uncommitted temp script with the host file-writing tool and run it with an explicit launcher. The finding payloads are agent-authored: summary/evidence text routinely contains apostrophes or other shell-special characters (e.g. "couldn't launch"), which break the single-quoted JSON and make the append command fail with JSON parse errors; on Windows cmd single quotes provide no quoting at all, so the recipe is not portable. Since this skill is the shipped contract for how orchestrators must call audit_log.js, a consumer agent following the recipe literally will corrupt or fail to log findings — the very defect the audit wrapper is meant to surface.

**Correção sugerida:**

```diff

-   node {skillsRoot}/ws-audit/scripts/audit_log.js append \
-     --session '{...}' \
-     --finding '{"step":"4",...}'
# With: write the finding JSON to a temp file with the file-writing tool,
# then run:
+   node {skillsRoot}/ws-audit/scripts/audit_log.js append \
+     --session-file "{us-dir}/.audit-session-{slug}.json" \
+     --finding-file "{us-dir}/.finding-step-4.json"

# + JSON.parse), keeping --session/--finding as-is for programmatic callers.
```
